title: Liberty Sanctuary in Heber Valley offers second chances for neglected, abandoned horses
text:

At Liberty Sanctuary in Heber Valley, horses that have been neglected, abandoned, or destined for kill pens are given a new life. “You feel like you are unlocking a life a life someone else was choosing to throw away,” West said.
At Liberty Sanctuary in Heber Valley, horses that have been neglected, abandoned, or destined for kill pens are given a new life. Since 2023, more than 40 horses have come through the sanctuary, where they receive care, rehabilitation and, ultimately, the opportunity to find a new home. For West, the mission is personal. After learning how many horses were ending up in kill pens, West felt compelled to act.
What began as a passion project has grown into a community effort. Today, Liberty Sanctuary relies on 75 volunteers who help care for the horses. Six horses have already been adopted this year alone.
“They need us as humans to take care of them and help put them in the right hands and help heal them,” she said. One example is 12-year-old Tatum and a horse named Max. The pair formed a special bond.
“We are giving Max to you,” West told her. “The two of them had made each other stronger and more confident in the world,” West said. The impact of West's work extends far beyond the horses she rescues. Through Liberty Sanctuary, she has built a community centered on compassion, healing, and second chances.
To recognize that impact, Mountain America Credit Union and KUTV surprised West with a Pay It Forward award and a donation to support her mission. Liberty Sanctuary is a horse rescue and rehabilitation organization based in Heber Valley that works to provide care, healing, and new homes for horses in need.
